desc: The council configuration layer: contexts (a small council, a Senate, a grand jury, a city board) are not different models but points in a configuration space of the one machine. RONR enumerates the axes itself. A configuration = parameter assignments along the axes + an overlay of patches against named model surfaces. The generic files state the ordinary-society defaults; the first named configuration below IS those defaults, extracted and named, so no context is implicit. Many councils, one engine. Axes are DOCUMENTATION (the book's own typology, with cites); params are the single OPERATIVE surface — a configuration's axes never bind anything an expression reads, so axis/param divergence is a description bug, not a behavior bug.

axes.desc: RONR's own principal types [1:9]; committees are subordinate instruments of an assembly, not assemblies [1:24]. Drives defaults on most other axes.

values: small (about a dozen or fewer present: the 49:21 relaxations)
axes.desc: small-board relaxations apply to small boards [49:21], to all standing/special committees unless instructed otherwise [50:25], and are adoptable by small societies as special rules [2:16 exceptions list, 49:21n]

values: call-as-bylaws (mass meeting: the call's purpose and invitees have bylaws force [53:9])
legislative stack (constitutions/statutes/chamber rules above any manual)
axes.desc: which documents exist above the parliamentary authority; parameterizes rules.json authority_order and which classes are populated

cascades into the quorum basis [40:2: (1) mass meeting = those present; (2) unreliable rolls = those who attend; (3) delegates = majority of registered; (4) enrolled = majority of members, absent a bylaw] and into vote bases (majority-entire-membership, majority-registered)

session shapes; term expiry — periodic partial replacement makes the board effectively a new board, dropping everything temporarily-but-not-finally disposed except committee referrals [49:22, 21:7(c)]; quarterly-interval relation gates carryover [9:7-10]

values: subordinate (board/committee of a society: instructable, ratifiable, overridable by the parent)
axes.desc: who instructs, who ratifies, who can discharge or override; a committee is accountable to a higher authority in a way no assembly is [1:24]; parent instruction displaces the 50:25 defaults ('unless the committee is otherwise instructed')

values: public body (sunshine laws open the meetings [9:28]; procedural statutes supersede and are unsuspendable [25:8]; compelled attendance / Call of the House where the body has the legal power [40:13])
axes.desc: populates rules.json class procedural-law and flips openness/attendance parameters

parameters.desc: Configuration parameters live at ctx.config (schema.json) and are consulted by expressions and by stage-5 orchestration. Types/defaults here; each named configuration assigns them.

list.type: boolean — chair debates and votes without leaving the chair
boolean — no make-window limit, two-thirds-with-drop threshold, mover = anyone not on losing side

overlay_mechanism.desc: A configuration applies, in order: (1) param assignments (into ctx.config); (2) patches — each {surface, op, ...} against a named model surface, applied at load, before any evaluation. The patched model is then evaluated exactly as the generic one. Note-grade entries (op: note) carry rule content the overlay has not compiled into expressions — they are flagged in gaps.json like any annotation-grade content.

ops.patch: {surface: dotted path into a model file, replace: new value/expression, cite}
ops.disable_motion: {motion, cite} — the registry record stays; the move action never offers it
ops.restrict_actions: {allowed: [action/motion ids], plus: [ids always retained], cite} — whitelist form: every motion/action not listed is disabled; the overlay shape for bodies the book defines by an enumerated permitted set rather than by deltas (committee of the whole [52:9])

configurations.desc: The extracted defaults: a local organized society, enrolled membership, periodic sessions within the quarterly corridor, full rule stack, private, autonomous, large-meeting formality. The generic model files ARE this configuration; it assigns every parameter its default and carries an empty overlay.
A board with not more than about a dozen members present [49:21]. The seven relaxations, compiled.

overlay.replace: on stated directly; the seconded state is skipped (no-second death transition also removed)

overlay.note: no limit on number or length of speeches — EXCEPT appeals, which keep the regular one-speech rule (chair twice)

action.note: when a proposal is perfectly clear to all present a vote may be taken without a motion; approval thresholds unchanged; initial show-of-hands allowed

overlay.surface: protocol.decorum: chair does not debate while presiding
overlay.replace: removed — the chair-member speaks in discussion and debate and votes on all questions without leaving the chair

overlay.desc: members raise a hand or remain seated to seek the floor, make motions, speak; chair need not rise to put the question — floor_formality=informal, consumed by protocol rendering

periodic partial replacement of board membership makes it a new board: everything temporarily-but-not-finally disposed falls to ground except committee referrals — already compiled as clock.term_boundary_before_next_session in guard/carryover-eligible

configurations.desc: A standing or special committee: a subordinate instrument, not an assembly [1:24]. The 49:21 relaxations apply unless the parent instructs otherwise [50:25], plus the committee-specific rule changes.

overlay.desc: reconsider under committee rules is already hooked in the generic model: no make-window limit (guard/within-reconsider-window's body_kind disjunct [37:35(1)]), mover = anyone not on the losing side, two-thirds threshold dropping to majority when all prevailing-side voters are present or notified [37:35(3)] (registry vote_notes); rescind/amend-adopted's committee thresholds likewise [35:2(7)]
the parent's instruction displaces any of this configuration ('unless the committee is otherwise instructed') — an authority-relation override, not a rules.json suspension

configurations.desc: The assembly itself acting as a committee [52]. Third proof configuration: §52 defines it by an enumerated permitted set, compiled as a whitelist.

overlay.note: the only motions in order are adopt (within the committee, for its report — the in-committee adopt is the rise-and-report content path), amend, and rise — plus, among incidentals, point of order, appeal, division of the assembly, and applicable requests and inquiries. Anything else requires rising to report a recommendation

action.note: rise (or rise-and-report): seconded, undebatable, unamendable, majority; always in order except during voting/verification or when another has the floor — the committee's only exit

overlay.replace: no limit on the number of speeches per member (the 49:21(3) relaxation as inherited), unless the assembly prescribed limits before going into committee of the whole

overlay.desc: quorum is the assembly's unless otherwise provided; on losing it, rise and report [52:18]; speeches in committee of the whole do not count against same-day assembly rights [13:21] (compiled in protocol counter rules); call-for-orders-of-the-day additionally barred generically via the body_kind disjunct in its applicability row [18:6]

configurations.desc: Unorganized assembly: whoever attends within the call's terms is a member; the call has bylaws force. Partial configuration.

overlay.replace: populated by the call: its statement of purpose and of who is invited has bylaws force — it bounds germaneness of main motions and defines membership

overlay.desc: quorum is the number present at the time [40:2(1)]; appeal of recognition rulings unavailable [42:15]; sponsors' rights shape presiding arrangements [53]

configurations.desc: A body of credentialed delegates, one session, with convention standing rules. Partial configuration.

overlay.desc: membership is established by adoption of the credentials report; until then only its consideration, conduct-of-meeting motions, and the inquorate set are in order [59:22]; convention-standing-rules class active with its suspension/threshold rows (rules.json); agenda/program overlay typically governs (scheduler.json)

configurations.desc: Constitutionally constituted, continuous or long sessions, inverted rule stack (constitutions and statutes above any manual), compelled attendance available. Sketch — RONR describes this type but is not its authority [1:9(4)].

action.note: unexcused absentees brought under arrest; not applicable in voluntary societies

overlay.desc: procedural statutes populate class procedural-law: supreme and unsuspendable unless self-suspending [25:8]; the body's own adopted rules displace most of the generic model — this configuration marks the axes, it does not model any particular chamber

configurations.desc: Overlay-only configuration (composable with board/committee/ordinary-society): a governmental or semi-public body under public law.

overlay.desc: sunshine laws override the assembly's power to exclude nonmembers or enter executive session [9:28]; applicable procedural statutes are unsuspendable [25:8] — both land in rules.json class procedural-law with continuing-breach ground violates-procedural-law [23:6(c)]

proof_note: small-board and committee are the proof configurations: every 49:21 item and every 50:25 delta is either compiled (param/patch/disable/add) or explicitly note-grade with its citation — nothing silently absorbed. The generic model needed zero changes to host them beyond ctx.config, which is the axes working as claimed: the hooks (body_kind disjuncts, term-boundary clock field, committee threshold notes) were already load-bearing in the ordinary-society model.
